englishOptions.text: Service actions

englishOptions.text: Sustainability

questions.sourceExplanation: Service actions are actions “performed by a service provider or jointly by a service provider and a service consumer. questions.englishQuestion: What influences whether a service is perceived as valuable by a consumer?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: The service provider’s ability to minimize their operational costs

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: The number of providers delivering the service to the consumer

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: The extent to which the positive effects of the service outweigh the negative ones

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: The amount of money the service provider invests in resources

questions.sourceExplanation: Services can introduce new costs and risks, and in some cases, they can negatively affect some of the intended outcomes, while supporting others. Services are valuable when the positive effects outweigh the negative ones. Ref 3.1.1

questions.englishQuestion: Which of the following is TRUE regarding services and desired outcomes?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Services guarantee that all intended outcomes will be achieved

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Services completely eliminate risks associated with achieving outcomes

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: Services always result in positive effects without exceptions

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Services may have unintended and surprising outcomes, both positive and negative

questions.sourceExplanation: When enabling desired outcomes for service consumers, services may also prevent or reduce other desired outcomes or introduce undesired ones […] In addition to the intended and anticipated positive and negative effect on service consumers, services may have unintended and surprising outcomes, both positive and negative. Ref 3.1.1

questions.englishQuestion: According to the ‘Focus on value’ ITIL Guiding Principle, all organizational activities should link back to what?

englishOptions.label: A

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Increased revenue only

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: Employee satisfaction

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Market share dominance

questions.sourceExplanation: The ‘Focus on value’ principle stipulates that all “activities conducted by the organization should link back, directly or indirectly, to value for itself, its customers, and other stakeholders.” Ref 5.2.1

questions.englishQuestion: According to the ITIL Guiding Principle ‘Start where you are’, what is the MAIN risk of starting over without considering what is already available when improving a service?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Losing opportunities for collaboration and shared understanding across teams

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Overcomplicating solutions by ignoring practical, simple approaches

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: Failing to gather feedback needed to guide gradual improvement

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Wasting time and losing valuable existing capabilities and resources

questions.sourceExplanation: When improving products or services, starting over completely is rarely wise. The approach of completely removing what has been done “can be extremely wasteful, not only in terms of time, but also in terms of the loss of existing capabilities, competencies, people, and tools that could have significant value in the improvement effort. Do not start over without first considering what is already available to be leveraged.” Ref 5.2.2

questions.englishQuestion: What is the MAIN purpose of using feedback throughout improvement iterations?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: To confirm that all stakeholder opinions are in agreement

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: To ensure that improvement actions remain relevant and effective in changing circumstances

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: To prevent the need for further adjustments once work has started

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: To avoid changes in project priorities during implementation

questions.sourceExplanation: Faster response to customer needs is one of the benefits of embedding feedback loops. “Working in a timeboxed, iterative manner with feedback loops embedded into the workflow allows for […] faster responses to customer and business needs” Ref 5.2.3.2

questions.englishQuestion: A design team is creating a new workflow and tries to account for every possible exception. What is the consequence of designing the workflow in this way?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Achieving stronger overall risk control

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Creating unnecessary complexity

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: Delivering outcomes more quickly and consistently

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Ensuring employees always follow processes without question

questions.sourceExplanation: Trying to provide a solution for every exception will often lead to over-complication. When creating a product or a practice, designers need to think about exceptions, but they cannot cover them all. Instead, they should design rules that can be used to handle exceptions generally. Ref 5.2.6

questions.englishQuestion: Why should organizations consider the interaction of ITIL Guiding Principles?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Because principles are interdependent and complement each other

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Because one principle is always superior to the rest

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: Because principles must be applied in a strict order

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Because one principle is usually suficient for any situation

questions.sourceExplanation: In addition to being aware of the ITIL Guiding Principles, it is important to recognize that they interact with and depend upon each other. For example, if an organization is committed to progressing iteratively with feedback, it should also think and work holistically to ensure that each iteration of an improvement includes all the elements necessary to deliver real results. Similarly, making use of appropriate feedback is key to collaboration, and focusing on what will truly be valuable to the customer makes it easier to keep things simple and practical. Ref 5.2.8

questions.englishQuestion: A printer is delivered to a customer, while ongoing maintenance and support are provided by the supplier. Which combination of service interactions is shown in this situation?

questions.sourceExplanation: The printer being delivered is a transfer of goods, while the ongoing maintenance and support provided by the supplier represent service actions. questions.englishQuestion: How does ‘access to resources’ support value co-creation in a service interaction?

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: By limiting resource use to internal teams

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: By replacing service actions with automation

questions.sourceExplanation: In ITIL, access to resources is a specific form of service interaction where the service consumer uses the service provider’s resources under agreed conditions. This access enables value co-creation because consumers can achieve outcomes without owning or managing those resources. “Access to resources: the service consumer gains access to the service provider’s resources and uses them according to the agreed terms and conditions.” Ref 3.1.2

questions.englishQuestion: Which of the following is TRUE about value co-creation?

englishOptions.label: D

questions.englishQuestion: How do ‘utility’ and ‘warranty’ together support value co-creation?

englishOptions.text: Utility and warranty apply only to products, not services

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Utility ensures the service is fit for purpose, while warranty ensures it is fit for use

questions.sourceExplanation: Utility and warranty are two complementary aspects of service value. Utility describes what the service does (fitness for purpose), while warranty describes how the service performs (fitness for use). questions.englishQuestion: Why does ITIL consider outcomes, costs, and risks together when explaining value co-creation?

englishOptions.text: Because outcomes eliminate the need to manage costs and risks

englishOptions.text: Because risks are more important than outcomes

questions.sourceExplanation: ITIL explains value co-creation as a balance between outcomes, costs, and risks. These three elements must be considered together to understand whether a service is truly valuable. Ref 3.1.1

questions.englishQuestion: What is service quality most concerned with?

questions.englishQuestion: What is the final step in the value stream mapping process?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Identify the stream.

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Map the "as-is" stream.

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: Plan and implement improvements

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Analyze the stream.

questions.sourceExplanation:
Value stream mapping is a technique used to visualize and analyze the flow of work and information. The process follows a structured sequence of five steps:
1. Identify the value stream: Determine which stream needs to be analyzed.
2. Map the ‘as-is’ stream: Document the current state of the workflow as it exists.
3. Analyse the stream: Look for waste (non-value-adding activities) and opportunities for optimization.
4. Map the ‘to-be’ stream: Design the desired future state of the workflow.
5. Plan and implement improvements: This is the final step, where the organization actually executes changes to achieve the target state.

questions.englishQuestion: Integrating ITIL and PRINCE2 ensures alignment between:

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Marketing and Sales only.

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Strategy, change initiatives, and operations

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: The office building and the parking lot.

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Junior staff and their families.

questions.sourceExplanation: Integrating ITIL and PRINCE2 creates a smooth flow from high-level vision to project delivery to daily support.

questions.englishQuestion: Which framework offers "agile, continuous development" practices?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: PRINCE2

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Governance

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: DevOps

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: The 6C Model

questions.sourceExplanation: DevOps is synonymous with agile methodologies in a technology context.

audit.classificationNote: Recall of which framework offers a capability.

questions.englishQuestion: PRINCE2 supports the "transition" of project outputs into:

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Physical trash.

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Managed, valuable services

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: Another project that never ends.

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: A technical manual that no one reads.

questions.sourceExplanation: In PRINCE2, the purpose of a project is to deliver outputs that are transitioned into outcomes and benefits.

questions.englishQuestion: Large or complex initiatives often require comprehensive methods like:

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Checking a single box on a list.

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Sending a single email to all staff.

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: PRINCE2 Project Management

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Guessing what to do next.

questions.sourceExplanation: Complexity requires a structured approach to manage risks, budgets, and timelines.

questions.englishQuestion: How does DevOps enhance "execution" in the value chain?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Through automation, collaboration, and fast feedback

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: By making every task manual.

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: By preventing teams from talking to each other.

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: By avoiding the use of metrics.

questions.sourceExplanation: DevOps principles match perfectly with ITIL guiding principles like "Collaborate" and "Progress Iteratively".

questions.englishQuestion: The ultimate goal of integrating ITIL, DevOps, and PRINCE2 is to deliver:

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: The most expensive services possible.

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Resilient, adaptive, and customer-focused services

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: A collection of documents that are never used.

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Services that never change for 50 years.

questions.sourceExplanation: Framework integration allows organizations to be agile enough to change while remaining stable enough to trust.

questions.englishQuestion: How do ITIL and DevOps work together?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: ITIL provides structure and governance; DevOps enables rapid development

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: They are competitors and cannot be used at the same time.

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: DevOps is used for small companies; ITIL is only for large ones.

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: ITIL replaces the need for any technical operational practices.

questions.sourceExplanation: Together, they balance the need for stability (ITIL) with the need for speed (DevOps).

questions.englishQuestion: Which BEST explains why an organization might choose to utilize external suppliers?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: To maintain greater control and visibility over service delivery

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: To minimize reliance on third-party providers

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: To remove the need for oversight, governance, and internal management

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: To obtain capabilities that are difficult to develop internally

questions.sourceExplanation: Organizations may utilize external suppliers due to resource scarcity, which includes a lack of needed skills or resources internally. It also allows them to leverage the subject matter expertise and knowledge of the supplier.

audit.classificationNote: Reasons for using external suppliers (partners and suppliers dimension).

questions.englishQuestion: Why is project management important in ITIL?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: To manage routine operational activities and service requests

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: To define governance authority across the ITIL Value System

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: To deliver time-bound initiatives that introduce new or changed services

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: To enable structured delivery of change while services continue to operate

questions.sourceExplanation: Project management is essential for delivering change within the ITIL Value System. Effective projects ensure that delivery is structured, controlled, and strategically aligned. PRINCE2 methods specifically support the delivery of changes that implement or modify products and services.

questions.englishQuestion: A telecom provider designs an enterprise package that contains internet, VoIP, network security, and technical support. Which concept does this illustrate?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Transfer of goods

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Service action

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: Access to resources

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Service offering

questions.sourceExplanation: A service offering is a formal description of one or more services designed to address the needs of a target consumer group, and it can include goods, access to resources, and service actions.

questions.englishQuestion: What is the purpose of the ITIL AI Capability Model?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: To describe how service providers, service consumers, and other parties interact with AI to co-create value

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: To describe how organizations can assess and develop capabilities for effective use of AI

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: To prescribe specific AI technologies required for service development and management

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: To measure the performance of AI-enabled services against predefined service levels

questions.sourceExplanation: The ITIL AI Capability Model helps outline AI's functional capabilities (like the 6C model) and connects them with assessing existing capabilities to address any gaps with clear action plans.

questions.englishQuestion: Which value chain activity is addressed by evaluating the quality of the resources and services sourced from a third party?

englishOptions.label: A
englishOptions.text: Build

englishOptions.label: B
englishOptions.text: Design

englishOptions.label: C
englishOptions.text: Acquire

englishOptions.label: D
englishOptions.text: Discover

questions.sourceExplanation: The "acquire" activity has specific success metrics, one of which is the quality of resources and services obtained.
